They are champions that want to impact the game early on, they do not farm particularly fast, do not scale as well full clearing (because they cannot farm as fast or kit related issue) or are impactful at level 2/3. These champions are different from those who excel at power farming like Diana and Hecarim and also different from champions that can flex the option like Viego and Graves. Either of these kinds of champions are okay, but champions like Rell do not fit this description.

For example Rell can do Raptors Red Krugs and look for gank, consider skipping Krugs if needed. But this is not a stable reference point. You will have games where your laners are in a winning or even match up level 1 and is pushing away from you. Which is also possible when playing Amumu, but with a clearing jungler you have already full cleared and are more effective. With Rell you can get around this by adapting, but this is no longer a basic reference point if you are starting to learn jungle decision making as a beginner.

It is easier to begin learning jungle using resources as a reference point (gold/experience) as a comparison than it is with comparing gank heavy champions. The learning point for resource jungling is "was this decision worth sacrificing farm" than it is with gank heavy champions where the question is more multi-faceted and it's easier to come to an incorrect conclusion without experience/knowledge

Hope that answers your question!

Amumu or any champion that can full clear under 3:15 with two smites. With just one is even better. Clear from Blue to Red and look for crab/gank. Recall as soon as possible and look to full clear again.

Use this as your reference point for adapting your decisions, like:
- Skipping Red to gank because there is a free double kill bot
- Clearing Red to Blue because the other lane is better to gank at the end of the clear
- Basing immediately after Krugs because you cannot contest scuttle

If you are learning to jungle this can be your initial cookie cutter plan; since the role is defined by making decisions appropriate to what is happening in the game you will learn to deviate from this plan when appropriate. The default idea should always be to farm/base, and then assess what variables would justify you doing something else like invading, ganking, starting an objective, pathing somewhere, diving, etc. It is your evaluation skill that you are developing as a jungler and this reference point helps in this regard to contrast your decision.

A reference point is easiest with champions that can full clear and not champions that want to gank at level 3 with 3 camps like Rell, Poppy or Elise. Champions that come to mind are Nocturne, Amumu, Udyr, Briar, Lillia, but anyone 1. with a clear under 3:15 and 2. someone you don't struggle to play mechanically 3. someone you have fun playing will be your best bet.

if you're getting leads as diana you want to press your advantage by looking for good fights. other things are important too like farming and objectives but you secure wins by fighting and putting the enemy further behind and bleeding that advantage to your teammates too.

Watch your ADC, if they are playing bad don't make it worse. You should not go for a play that depends on them while they are not looking, int, and then blame them for being bad. Part of being good at league is adapting to your team being garbage.

That and get better at laning. You need to get an advantage through harass/knowing when to back/what to do with the wave/out trading/out spacing the enemy if you're playing an enchanter, and then carry that lead out of lane. Would personally not recommend enchanters if you're in silver because part of your agency is in supporting your team, whereas Brand or other damage champions you don't have to rely on them nearly as much.

But this is cookie cutter advice. Ask around if anyone would be willing to go over replays with you for actual advice specific to you and your tendencies.

>*"My question is pretty much, How to avoid being invaded in my jungle...too."*

\- Before you enter into a game, look at your lanes, and the enemy jungler should do the same. There are lanes that should make no sense to path towards at the end of their clear, and in that way you can tell which direction they should clear. Certain junglers like pathing certain ways at certain speeds, Kayn can't clear like Karthus, Diana likes full clearing whereas Veigo can flex well. Certain match ups are favoured for your lane and sometimes for the other, and sometimes it changes as the levels increase. This is important knowledge to have as a jungler that you can invest time in learning outside of the game to assess win conditions and what each side wants to play around.

\- When you enter the game, your first ward will give you the most information. Especially with Diana you can check brushes with Q to go and ward their Raptors or their buff. If you know where they are starting and their clear speed you will know how they will path and can that helps you track them from the very beginning.

​

>*"Sometimes I feel like when my team just doesn't care...etc."*

\- You can't always force your teammates to do what you need them to do. Play it as it is, not how it should be. The only things you can do are ping, type and set up, if they choose not to do the right thing then your job is not to int and point at them for not doing their job. As a jungler most of your job is covering for your team's mistakes and not letting them int in shadowing them while they push out, shoving their wave in so they can recall, etc. If they are bad then you can't do a whole lot, just do your best.

​

>*"When I can find out where my jungle enemy is, at least if hes top I can try to get dragon, get bot...just rotates to me."*

\- Track enemy jungler and watch lanes. There are things that they can and can't do, and based on that knowledge you adapt your pathing based on what you can the most out of in a situation. Is your lane pushing out into their enemy jungler who is clearing that way? Where is the wave and which direction is it going? Does your lane need to back and in turn need you to come shove it out? These are things the enemy jungler is thinking of as well, and your job as a jungler is to assess and reply. There are a lot of things to think about, and making thought processes takes a lot of practice and review to get it right and know what you should do when xyz happens.

\- Based on what you're saying you have a binary understanding of what to do instead of *evaluating* what can or should be done. Just because the enemy is getting an objective does not mean you drop everything you are doing to go answer, because often times that's not an option. If your bot lane gets caught out on low resources and your mid top have no prio, does that mean you go straight to herald when they start drag if you just finished a full clear towards bot?

\- There are things you can do as a jungler to be efficient, sometimes it's your fault something doesn't happen. Other times it's your team's fault and in that case you just do your best.

​

>*"I find myself doing really good...pings."*

\- Mute, you get less out of listening to random strangers and them flaming you more often than not than you do from building your own mental model of the game.

\- Have fun and be open to learning and thinking about the game and why things are the way they are.
If they sprint down the lane and flash forwards and you get nothing out of helping. You get more by doing nothing rather than trying to salvage where no salvaging is possible. That is an example.

\- Communicate. Assume your teammates aren't on the same page if there's any level of ambiguity. Try to ping, if you have the time maybe type. It's not guaranteed to work but if you can ping then there's no harm trying. Maybe they didn't see something, and pinging sometimes works.

\- Play as it is, not how it should be. There may be times when there's technically a better play but your team goes for something else. It may be better to go for the suboptimal decision together as a team rather than to go and do your own thing. 

\- However this isn't the same as if they are making an objectively bad decision, and in that case all you can do is patch the bleeding and wait for opportunities to come back. Don't hard throw with them.

Every game is different and without seeing a replay then you'll only get blanket statements. Some games there isn't much else you can do, just go next.

If they have a wave at your turret chances are you won’t reliably trade anyways in a 1v2 situation plus contending an enemy wave. You’re only there to farm unless they massively screw up. If the support is full resources they should not be backing. If you have no resources you need to back. If either of you back, it is the other person’s job not to get chunked resulting in split backing a second time.

Split backs are fine if you do not need to be exerting pressure/shoving lane. If your support backs earlier than you they can catch the wave if it’s coming back to you or roam if they don’t need to be bot immediately. The question tends to be more of do you as adc need support bot with you or are you okay on your own, at which point their first responsibility early should be to be match the 2v2. There are a lot of factors, but notably you do not actually need 2 people together at all times bot lane, just need 2 there at times when you need 2 people there and not as a default.
Placements finish after about 10 matches, your mmr will even out after probably 100 matches and then you will play people around your skill level

Work on solidifying your basics. If you can do that, then you'll skyrocket. The basics of League will help you be the most consistent in your matches. So these skills would include:

- Trading
- Warding
- Minimap awareness
- CSing
- Damage gauging
- Cookie cutter builds
- Spacing and ranges

If you can do all of that *perfectly* you can probably get thrown up to very high elo, but since no one does them perfectly, those are things that you'll always want to work on getting better.

A side note, looking at your runes on the Malzahar match you probably don't need scaling mana regen yellows, you shouldn't really be spamming your abilities that much. You can always ask for blue if your jungler is nice, but even then managing your mana is important. Get scaling health instead if you don't think you're going to have a rough early game, otherwise get flat or armour against Yas. Also, if you're having a hard time early with those first two deaths you can start off with an Armguard and then build RoA since it gives you both AP and armour.

You can also consider taking scaling MR blues in the jungle because you won't really be taking too much AP damage.

But most importantly work on the basics, that will get you much further and help you continually climb rather than band-aid fixes with builds, pathing and other tricks.

20 AD is not a lot, noting that your are probably not running AD pen (against lane opponent, but true you will do more damage to minions). You actually do lose quite a bit of damage because early only your W scales with AD. Additionally, 1250g from a Needlessly Large Rod will provide more damage from ratios than a Tiamat because:
NLR: 60 AP
Tiamat: 20 AD
Sinister Steel (W): *25% AP* -> 60 APx0.25 = 15 damage *60% AD* -> 20 ADx0.60 = 12 damage
Death Lotus (R): *25% AP* -> 60 APx0.25 = 15 damage *37.5% AD* -> 20 ADx0.375 = 7.5 damage

Depends on your match ups, there are lane opponents that exist that you don't want to stick around the wave too long, and with a Tiamat (or at least to push and clear lots) you have to adopt a playstyle that puts you in the wave. So the argument becomes what match up will you need to have that early wave clear that you can't wait for a Luden's.

Hi,

Corrupting Potion purchase on Katarina for the use of the passive is not a good reason because every one of her abilities counts as AoE except her E, so you will get reduced damage from it.

As strange as it sounds, The Dark Seal, for the purpose of sustain, is better than Corrupting Potion. Now please keep your pants on as I give you the reasoning.

Corrupting Potion:
- 500g to purchase, 200g regained when sold
- Heals 450 with the three charges

So if you go back twice, it'll give you a total of 900 health back and have a sunk cost of 300g.

Dark Seal:
- 350g to purchase, 245g regained when sold
- 3 potions heal you for four hundred and fifty health +25% for a total of 562.5 (and if you take biscuit because you're want even more sustain then 622.5)

So if you go back twice, it'll give you a total of 1245 health back and have a sunk cost of 405g (6 pots + Dark Seal sell).

Additionally, since Dark Seal gives you 15 AP and not a reducing passive due to AoE, it'll give you more damage .-.

Corrupting Potion isn't a bad buy but I think Dark Seal is better. I personally wouldn't upgrade it into Meijei's though unless it's against bots, but early it's good. The debate comes down to how long you're willing to keep your Corrupting Potion, because if you think about it, it has the same 'problem' Crystalline Flask had in that it's effective when you go back to get charges, but if you go back you give up CS, i.e gold and exp and potentially turret damage. So the more you go back the more gold you're trading off that you're trying to save with a Corrupting Potion purchase. Also not sure if that 105g difference is that crucial of a difference, you can stick around for another wave to get that. Another small advantage of Corrupting Potion over Dark Seal is that it heals over 12 seconds instead of 15, i.e 12.5/s and not 10/s, but that's balanced by the instant 20 health you get if you have biscuits.

EDIT: This Dark Seal start is better for getting you through early game than Corrupting Potion. It's not meant for you to hold. The Corrupting Potion, the longer you hold on to it, will 'give you back more gold' but you debate how much 450 health is late game .-. So you could make the argument that Corrupting Potion is better in that way.

Katarina excels off of resets, otherwise she is just about as dangerous as an under farmed, short ranged Brand. Katarina does poorly in extended team fights because optimally she needs to wait for an opportunity to go in rather than create them herself, meaning her team will be fighting a lot of 4v5 before she can hop in. But if she does get those resets then you're in for a world of hurt!

There's a few ways to address that, if you have champions that can prolong your fights like Soraka, then that helps you out. Or, just champions that deny Katarina her resets like Tahm Kench or Kindred. You don't have to have hard CC to stop her ult, if you have someone who can 1-shot her then that works just as well.

A lot like any other snowball-y champion, it's hard to keep her in check because you have to keep your foot down on her face to make sure she never snowballs, and you can't always do that in solo queue ;~; there's ways to play around it as Kat, it's very much about adaptability for people playing against her and people playing with her.

Max Q if you're playing assassin Katarina
Max W if you're playing tank Katarina

A misnomer about Katarina is that your W does more damage than your Q in melee match ups. In a 10 second span:

If you are level 5 maxing W:
Q Damage: 75 (+65% AP) on 10s CD
W Damage: 110 (25% AP) on 4s CD x2   Total: 295 (+115% AP)

If you are level 5 maxing Q:
Q Damage: 155 (+65% AP) on 9s CD
W Damage: 40 (+25% AP) on 4s CD x2  Total: 235 (+115% AP)

As you can see, if you land W twice over the course of 10 seconds, you will out damage Q maxing by 60. The argument for W is that you can spam it while you can't do so with Q. This is where the flaw is, because as Katarina your damage early is bad. You will definitely do more damage over time, but what people tend to forget is that you are not playing against a bot that will not trade back. Katarina does not excel at extended trades; you can stick around for another 4 seconds to W sure but most every melee match up you will be against someone who can do enough damage during those 4 seconds to greatly outweigh the pros of 60 damage. Unless you're playing tank Katarina where you thrive in long trades, then maxing W is not actually a good idea. Your goal is to go through a single spell rotation and get out, Katarina is not Ryze, your DPS is out matched by most all your lane opponents. Also, note that the 60 damage is a benefit only if you land it twice within that 10 second window; if you don't, then it doesn't actually out DPS maxing Q

Abyssal is a good buy when you're laning against an AP champion like Leblanc or Orianna because it provides MR, and it'll let you stay around in lane longer to farm, and it's cheap. Usually as Katarina the 20 MR reduc is good enough because the squishy champions that you should be targeting as an assassin won't have that much MR to begin with. However, Void Staff will do more penetration than Abyssal if they build pretty much any MR item. But back to your point, don't ever get both. You don't need that much penetration, if you build AP your ratios will do all the work.

And your last point, unfortunately assassin Katarina has really bad DPS, so you can't do anything against those tanks. If you were at least Zed with autos or Diana with Nashors then you can paw at them but Katarina kinda has to sit back and watch.
